title: Legend clustering, high-contrast token map, and keyboard cluster navigation for dense time-series
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Our time-series charts often display dozens of series for operational customers. The current legend renders one DOM entry per series which causes layout thrash and is overwhelming for keyboard and screen reader users. Additionally, color tokens produce low-contrast elements when many series are present and token selection is not density-aware.

Goal: Introduce a legend clustering strategy that groups visually similar or related series into interactive clusters, provide a density-aware color token map with guaranteed contrast ratios for cluster summaries, and add a keyboard-first navigation pattern that lets users traverse clusters and then drill into individual series. This should reduce DOM surface area, improve performance for high-density charts, and meet WCAG 2.1 AA for text/icon contrast in legend items and cluster summaries.
acceptance_criteria: Legend clusters collapse when > 12 series in viewport; cluster headers show aggregated mini-sparkline and series count
Color token mapping includes a density fallback palette: when series > 8 use high-contrast monotone accents with distinct pattern/hatch overlays for printed/exported charts

Keyboard navigation: Tab focuses cluster controls; ArrowRight/ArrowLeft moves between clusters; Enter expands cluster to a focusable list of series; ArrowDown/ArrowUp navigate within expanded series list
SR (screen reader) behavior: cluster expand/collapse announced via aria-live; each cluster summary exposes a concise accessible name and aggregated statistics (min/max/latest) of the grouped series
Performance: initial legend render reduced DOM nodes by >= 70% on datasets with 50 series (measured in devtools), first-contentful-interaction for the legend <= 80ms on CI profile
Design tokens: new tokens introduced and documented in token map; migration docs for component library provided
Fallbacks: canvas-rendered legend option available behind feature flag for extreme density cases (>150 series)
Unit/e2e tests cover keyboard flows, aria announcements, and contrasts for all token combinations
tasks: Design: create token map for density-aware palettes and annotated Figma symbols
Design: prototype clustered legend micro-interactions and keyboard flows in Figma
Engineering: implement cluster algorithm (group by color similarity + metadata tag) in chart component
Engineering: add optional canvas legend renderer and feature flag
Accessibility review: run with screen reader (VoiceOver/NVDA) and produce ARIA pattern doc
Docs: write migration notes for design tokens and usage guidelines
QA: performance regression test against 50/150 series fixtures
decisions: Use cluster-first approach instead of virtualizing every legend item because virtualization breaks SR affinity and keyboard order
Color tokens: extend existing token set with --chart-dense-01..--chart-dense-06 and a pattern overlay token --chart-overlay-dots for non-color-reliant distinction
ARIA approach: clusters expose button with aria-expanded + aria-controls pointing to an inert list of series; live region summarizes expansion outcome
Performance: implement lazy hydration of expanded cluster items (render list only when expanded) and reuse DOM nodes where possible
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: clustering algorithm may group unrelated series if metadata is sparse; Mitigation: allow explicit series tagging via config and fall back to name-based heuristics
Risk: pattern overlays increase visual noise; Mitigation: only enable overlays in print/export or when user toggles 'high-contrast' mode
Risk: canvas fallback breaks text selection and tooltips; Mitigation: keep interactive overlay layer for pointer events and expose accessible summary nodes in DOM
